design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (primary_care_assignment, category pcp).

1. WHY A GOOD TEST. Desmond Achterberg-Nwosu asks for a second opinion from Dr. Hannah Okonjo-Pierce (NPI 1275940318) before the total knee replacement his surgeon requested. The scored answer is the second-opinion visits (7). The agent must read that the second opinion is recorded only after the current assignment carries a single referral, dated on or after its effective date, to the specialist whose recommendation is reviewed (for a surgery: the requesting provider on the surgical authorization request); find in the authorizations that PA-2609-318840 (submitted) was requested by 1790234516 (Dr. Soto); find in the PCP history that the only referral to Soto (RF-2506-22847, 2025-06-02) sits on the ended Standard assignment and predates the active assignment (effective 2026-02-01), while the active assignment carries only a dermatology referral; issue the single referral (8 visits, six factors) and then size the second opinion from it (review visits 8 // 4 = 2) plus three more factors.

2. SCOPE. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6,4]; single referral 6, second opinion 4. Task 0 occupies carry-over, standing and continuity policies and tools; task 1 claims pcp_ext_specialist_referral + issue_specialist_referral_96d4855f and pcp_ext_second_opinion + request_second_opinion_76735634. After task 1 all five policies are covered, scopes disjoint.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root pcp_ext_second_opinion (user tool). Edge: second opinion -> pcp_ext_specialist_referral, kind value_input, gate treating_visits, form state, sentence 'A second-opinion referral is recorded only after the current assignment carries a single referral, dated on or after the assignment's effective date, to the specialist whose recommendation is being reviewed.' (affirmative: a booking recorded only after). Four-point test: connective 'only after'; a record-visible state (a single-type referral entry on the active assignment with date >= effective date naming that specialist); no tool/id/code token; scope exactly one specialist. Unique writer: only the single-referral policy writes a new single referral dated today on the active assignment; carried referrals keep their pre-assignment dates, standing referrals are another type, continuity and second-opinion referrals name other providers. Unresolved at frozen_time: active assignment f774cdae-25ff-4b3d-b760-da38872e4a1c carries only RF-2603-36051 to dermatologist 1932750186; RF-2506-22847 to 1790234516 is on ended assignment 681e6d45-f04f-4ede-a49d-adf5ca46dfd2 and dated 2025-06-02. Deletion sensitivity (run): skip the referral -> second opinion 5 (not 7). The persona never names the referral; tools validate nothing.

4. FACTOR CARD. single referral (holding active PCMH, ceiling 12): core_visits [parameter, multi-source, auth+plan] 2 specialist claims in 12 months (2025-10-24, 2026-03-20; 2025-08-15, 2025-06-20 outside) AND surgical request submitted -> 8 (baseline 4 -> 5); result_review [parameter, multi-source, auth] imaging approved, rehabilitation expired (near miss) -> 1 (-> 7); travel_distance [parameter, ride] longest completed leg 17.5 mi, cancelled 58.2-mi leg excluded (near miss) -> 1 (-> 7); medication_review [parameter, rx] non-preferred celecoxib in 3 months, no specialty -> 1 (-> 7); emergency_followup [parameter, plan] 2026-06-12 emergency (2026-02-08 outside) -> 1 (-> 7); eligibility_alignment [method, plan] active, renewal 2027-05-31 = 8 whole months -> x 8/12 (unaligned -> 12). 12 x 8/12 = 8; all-baseline 4. second opinion (same holding): recommendation_review [method, auth + own history] submitted request -> treating visits 8 // 4 = 2 (baseline none -> 5); imaging_review [parameter, plan] 1 lab/x-ray claim in 3 months (06-10 outside) -> 1 (-> 6); controlled_medication [parameter, rx] 2 Schedule IV tramadol fills in 3 months (06-20 outside) -> 2 (-> 5); mobility_level [parameter, ride] RideLink Ambulatory Sedan -> 1 (-> 6). 1+2+1+2+1 = 7; all-baseline 1. No outcome stamp exists for any factor.

5. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Subject pcp_referral_issue, governed only by pcp_referrals; eligibility referral_from_active_pcp holds for both writes (assignment f774cdae-25ff-4b3d-b760-da38872e4a1c active, pre-action). No time gate. overwrite [] for both: 8 and 7 are within 'covers up to referral_max_visits' (12).

6. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Treating specialist = requesting provider of PA-2609-318840 (1790234516). The dermatology referral (1932750186) is excluded from treating_visits by the specialist filter; the old Soto referral is excluded because it sits on the ended assignment. Second-opinion specialist 1275940318 comes from the member.

7. WORLD ROWS. customer, Expansion Adult membership (active, renewal 2027-05-31), 2 pcp_assignments, 4 pcp_events (2 change logs, 2 referrals), 13 plan_claims (3 Soto, 1 dermatology, 4 PCP, 2 ER, 2 lab/x-ray, 1 MRI outpatient), rx coverage + 8 fills (celecoxib non-preferred, tramadol CIV, lisinopril), ride benefit (Ambulatory Sedan) + 4 trips (incl. the cancelled 58.2-mile leg), 3 authorizations (surgery submitted, MRI approved, PT expired). No pending assignment, no exit or dismissal notice: no automatic clause fires.

8. PERSONA. Friendly, wary of surgery, to the point. Volunteers only the goal (a second opinion from Dr. Okonjo-Pierce before agreeing to the knee surgery, set up today) and that he is not cancelling the surgery request or changing doctors. Identity on request (phone, DOB; Medicaid ID, SSN4, ZIP if more). Must-ask answers: the chosen doctor's NPI (from Bluestem's form), his PCP, visits wanted (whatever the plan covers). Passive: go ahead with anything needed on the file; submits the request himself with the values read to him; closes after the confirmation.

9. STANDARD SOLUTION (15 actions). find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone + DOB) -> memberships -> PCP assignments -> PCP events -> claims -> authorizations -> rx coverage -> fills -> ride benefit -> trips -> unlock/call issue_specialist_referral_96d4855f(active, 1790234516, 8) -> unlock_user/call_user request_second_opinion_76735634(active, 1275940318, 7).

10. VERIFICATION RUN. Scratch harness (check_compute evaluator on the replayed world): single 8 (baselines 5/7/7/7/7/12, all 4); second opinion 7 (5/6/5/6, all 1; skip referral 5; cross-off 1; history-zero 5). Gates --task 1: EXTENDED, TASK TOOL CONTRACT, REPLAY, SOLVABILITY, COMPUTE, GROUNDING, SCOPE all OK. Pitfalls a careless agent hits: treating the dermatology referral or the expired Soto referral as the treating referral (review 1 or 0), counting the cancelled 58-mile ride (travel 2), counting the expired PT authorization (review 2), skipping the eligibility alignment (12).

11. REVISIONS. pcp_visits rows were dropped from this world (no factor reads them, and an unread row breaks the replay closure). The eligibility alignment rounds with int(RND(x, 6)) to guard 12 x 8/12 against floating error.

12. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the two rules, the tool schemas and finder outputs alone: the second-opinion rule points at the requesting provider of the surgical request and at a referral dated on or after 2026-02-01, which does not exist -> issue it first; the single-referral rule's six tiers and alignment give 8; the second-opinion rule's submitted-request tier divides those 8 visits by 4. Same calls and values as gold.

13. REVISIONS ROUND 2 (policy-task audit round 1: task 1 PASS). Charter-wide changes touching this task, with no value change (recomputed: single 8, second opinion 7, all factor baselines as before): both rules now state that their windows are trailing whole-month periods with the anniversary date outside (O-G10); the two tool docstrings no longer point at lookups (O-G7). O-G12 (a non-pain Schedule IV fill), O-G14 (no multi-source factor in the second opinion; the task bound is met by core_visits and result_review) and O-T1-1 (in-network status of the chosen doctor not in records) left as observations: none has a consequence on this world.
user_scenario:
You are Desmond Achterberg-Nwosu, 55, a retired forklift driver in Lincoln with a bad left knee. You are friendly, a bit wary of doctors who want to cut, and you like to get to the point, though you tend to add a joke or two. Your orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Raymond Soto at the Seward Bone and Joint Clinic, told you that you need a total knee replacement, and his office said they sent the surgery paperwork to Prairie Ridge a couple of weeks ago. Before you agree to anything, you want a second opinion from another bone doctor, Dr. Hannah Okonjo-Pierce at Bluestem Orthopedics, whom a friend recommended. You open by saying that: you want a second opinion from Dr. Okonjo-Pierce before you agree to the knee surgery, and you want it set up today so you can book with her office. You are not cancelling the surgery request and you are not changing doctors; you just want the second opinion first.

You give your name when you start. When the representative asks for details to find or verify you, you give your phone number, 4025550862, and your date of birth, 1971-08-19; if they want more, your Medicaid ID is PR58204613, the last four of your Social Security number are 5391 and your ZIP code is 68502. If they ask for Dr. Okonjo-Pierce's NPI, you read it off the new-patient form Bluestem mailed you: 1275940318. You do not know any plan reference numbers and say so if asked. If asked who your primary care doctor is, you say Dr. Venkataraman at Capitol Beach, and that you switched to her at the start of the year. If asked how many visits you need with Dr. Okonjo-Pierce, you say you have no idea and will go with whatever the plan covers.

You are fine with the representative doing whatever has to be done on your record to make this work; if they explain that something needs to be put on your file first, you tell them to go ahead. Asking for the second opinion is your own call, so when the representative says you need to submit it yourself and gives you the details to enter, you enter exactly what they read out and read back the confirmation number you get. If they quote a number of visits, you take it. Once you have the confirmation number for the second opinion with Dr. Okonjo-Pierce, you thank them, say you will call Bluestem this afternoon, and hang up.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.pcp_assignment_id: f774cdae-25ff-4b3d-b760-da38872e4a1c. Basis: 'A single specialist referral is issued by the member's active assignment'; the only active assignment is f774cdae-25ff-4b3d-b760-da38872e4a1c (Dr. Venkataraman). The ended Standard assignment cannot issue (base: 'A referral is issued only on an assignment in active status').
argument_uniqueness_tracing.specialist_npi: 1790234516. Basis: the second-opinion rule waits on a referral 'to the specialist whose recommendation is being reviewed' and 'Where the recommendation under review is a surgery, the specialist whose recommendation is being reviewed is the requesting provider on the member's Elective Inpatient and Surgical Authorization request'; PA-2609-318840 lists requesting provider 1790234516 (Dr. Soto).
argument_uniqueness_tracing.referral_visits: 8 = min(12, int(12 x 8/12)). Core: 2 paid specialist claims in the 12-month look-back (2025-10-24 Soto, 2026-03-20 dermatology; 2025-08-15 and 2025-06-20 fall outside) >= active-use count 2 AND a surgical request in submitted status -> surgical-care visits 8. Review: approved Advanced Imaging yes, approved Outpatient Rehabilitation no (the PT authorization is expired) -> exactly one -> 1. Travel: longest completed medical leg 17.5 miles, at least the middle 15 but below the far 30 -> 1. Medication: no specialty fill but non-preferred celecoxib fills 2026-08-02 and 09-01 in 3 months -> 1. Emergency: 1 paid emergency claim in 6 months (2026-06-12; 2026-02-08 outside) -> 1. Total 12; membership active, renewal due 2027-05-31 = 8 whole months (< 12) -> x 8/12 = 8, rounded down 8; ceiling 12.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.referral_visits: 7 = min(12, 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1). Consultation 1. Review: the surgical request is in submitted status -> the visits recorded on the active assignment's single referrals to its requesting provider 1790234516 (the 8 just issued) divided by the visits-per-review count 4, rounded down = 2. Imaging review: 1 paid lab/x-ray claim in the 3-month work-up window (2026-08-05; 2026-06-10 outside) -> 1. Controlled medication: tramadol (Schedule IV) fills 2026-07-28 and 08-27 in 3 months (2026-06-20 outside) = 2 -> 2. Mobility: active RideLink Ambulatory Sedan -> 1. Sum 7, within ceiling 12.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: Single edge, so the topological order is unique. Recording the second opinion first would size it with treating_visits 0 (5 visits instead of 7), a different terminal state; only referral -> second opinion reproduces gold.
